tests_may_change_note: The listed test asserts the exact GET /files/{file_id} body, which gains two keys.

early_rules: 1 a ready file stays ready and answers from its current chunks until the new version is published
2 a failed replacement (terminal or budget spent) changes nothing and is reported
3 nothing staged is deleted; staging_ref moves only on publish
5 the filename changes only on publish
6 every upload is a numbered version 1, 2, 3 with no gaps; each ends published or failed, or is pending
7 files already in the database are version 1 with the outcome their status implies

naive_patches.naive-reupload.patch: treats a replacement like a re-upload: the ready file goes back to queued/processing while the new version runs (breaks rule 1)
naive_patches.naive-failure.patch: forgets the failure path in the worker: a failed replacement stays 'pending' for ever and is never reported (breaks rule 2)
naive_patches.naive-s3.patch: stages the upload before checking whether the request can be accepted, so a refused replacement leaves bytes in the staging folder (breaks rule 4); passes the acceptance tests
naive_patches.naive-backfill.patch: creates the version table but does not bring existing files into it (breaks rule 7)
